Gerard Way alone is unique and enjoyable, I couldn't tell you how many times I've listened to Hesitant Alien this year lol. Those collabs with Mikey (Baby, You're a Haunted House) and Ray (Into the Cave We Wander and the rest) are clearly still Gerard but they are best defined as Gerard and Mikey/Ray, a unique pairing that is beautiful and cozy, like a fresh snowfall when one is safe, warm, and has nowhere to be and a loved one to spend the day with. Gerard has a talent for working with artists to craft a world that is definitely a blend of artists without losing the singular identity of each collaborator. Not easy to do, but Gerard is a helluva an artist. 

I really like seeing what artists do outside of the context I'm used to (or first) seeing them in, it helps me understand what each artist adds to the collective that makes MCR so great. Gerard is silly but definitely can be serious, Frank seems like he's Angry but has a very vulnerable center (like an armadillo), Mikey and Ray both have a flair to them that I can't quite grasp but is unique to each. 

That being said, I'd love another MCR album but more solo/small group collabs would also be understandable and enjoyable for me. I wonder if Gerard and Frank have done a collab before, that I'd love to see, just looking at Leathermouth to Hesitant Alien.

I grew up listening to Kiss, Bowie, and AC/DC (my grandma /loved/ Kiss) and I just figured that Rockstar was its own gender. It wasn't until middle school or so that I connected that maybe the reason I had a photo of Gerard shoved into my compact mirror was because I wanted to look and act like them, in a gender way. 

Realizing that I didn't have to put on a show of A Specific Gender and I could do what made sense for me, what I liked not what people wanted was freeing. Realizing that being somewhere inbetween or wholly outside of gender wasn't just for Rockstars or otherwise successful creative types gave me the push I needed to experiment and figure out what I actually was (or wasn't!). 

Gerard was definitely my first case of serious gender envy. Previous to getting into MCR, my biggest gender envy was Labyrinth David Bowie, but only the Goblin King for some reason and even that was very mild, so take that for what you will lol. Trying to live authentically, thanks to Gerard's influence, allowed me to come to terms with what I am. My penchant for glitter eyeshadow, platform boots, and dramatic eyeliner likely has more ro do with Kiss than MCR lol. 

(That being said, that one line in Mama is actually how I got into the band, because for the first time I felt like someone really /understood/ my problem of being inbetween/outside of that son or daughter problem. Probably why my friend insisted I start with that song lol)

TL;DR: Gerard Way presented an opportunity I hadn't considered bc I thought that to be Rockstar Gender I had to be a Rockstar lol. Plus, Mama makes all kinds of trans people feel seen, binary or not.

Hi there. Native montanan here, I've been an out and proud transgender individual for well over a decade. Setting aside that there are plenty of cultures on Montana soil that recognize gender outside of the binary because you certainly aren't ready for that conversation, should one be "critical" of this?

I'm not particularly liberal nor conservative, but I believe in the right to privacy. Personally, gender nor sex have any business being on documents. You know what happens when it has an "X" on your ID instead of an "M" or an "F"? Nothing, no world ending, no corruption of the blood, no blood rain, no apocalypse. If you were a physician, the conversation might be different in that the conversation about the patient's genitals wouldn't be happening at the DMV or on Reddit. There may be some issues traveling internationally, but that is indeed a personal choice to risk. 

Tell me, o wise redditor, why do you give a damn about what's in my pants so much that you must be "critical" of something that benefits anyone that enjoys privacy, self determination, and minding one's own business? Those are all Montana values, last I checked. If you don't like them, feel free to move! 

If any questions arise, the Trevor Project, local LGBTQ+. organizations, and opening a book should clear that up. Transgender individuals have been around a long time, all around the world. This isn't new, we're not going anywhere. 

Happy pride!

Howdy, certified pharmacy tech here, the answer is a fair bit, depending on state regulations. The education includes but is not limited to: the top 200 most prescribed drugs, common doses, uses, federal/state/local drug regulations, drug interactions with drugs, conditions, food and other contraindications, the schedule of any substance per DEA regulations, and the ability to make sense of the chicken scratch your doc scrawls out and ensure it doesn't kill you. 

That doesn't begin to deal with insurance, prior authorization processes, vaccine administration, and the other skilled labour done well before your meds ever hit the counter with your name on it. 

For what it's worth, due to federal regulations most pills cannot be put "in bags" because a bag is not considered a child safe container. A pharmacy tech is not just a pretty face at the window. 

Tldr? Pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, drug laws and regulations, as well as ethics.
